findings.title: Denial assertions do not prove zero changed rows
findings.body: state(..., preparation=True) snapshots the full S01 row but only counts rows in preparation/publication/receipt/event/outbox and other target tables. Most basis and authentication denial cases compare this count snapshot, so changing an existing S21/S22/S23, S24/S25 or bookkeeping row without changing counts can pass. The preparation_basis_denials_dc oracle explicitly requires zero new rows/changed rows, and immutable history must remain intact. Use complete persisted-row snapshots for all relevant existing tables around each denial; history() already demonstrates full-row comparisons for only a subset of cases.

findings.title: Positive pipeline lacks independent persisted hash/reference assertions
findings.body: test_owner_pipeline checks the stored S21 revision and S22 count, then checks T3 counts/pointer/generation. It does not independently derive and compare the persisted S21 content/basis/provenance, each S22 positive and collection/absence reference/window/signature, complete BUILDING and READY S23 candidate hashes/roles/artifact closure, or exact S24/S25 identities and refs from actual source rows. T3 success provides substantial guard coverage, but the packet additionally requires exact persisted hashes/refs/roles/artifact closure derived from the sealed admitted inputs. Assertions derived only from returned outcomes or production helper computations would not satisfy that independent oracle.

findings.title: Duplicate contenders do not assert exact persisted immutable closure
findings.body: The three races observe pg_blocking_pids and require equal returned outcomes. After each race they do not assert exactly one corresponding immutable S21 result with complete S22 closure, exactly one S23 build/local READY transition, or unchanged byte-identical winner content. Equal API results alone cannot establish the preparation_duplicate_rollback_dc one-result/dependency-closure/build and no-overwrite oracle. Add exact persisted row sets/counts and immutable candidate comparisons after releasing each observed blocker.
